newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks trend lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks trend lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks shed nearly 100 points of recent gains in early morning trade, in what brokers said was a bout of healthy consolidation.
"After seven days of advances, this is just a healthy consolidation,"said Boby Ho, dealing manager at G.K.Goh Securities.
The Hang Seng Index slipped 95.02 points in the first 30 minutes to trade at 11,526.59, a decline of 0.82 percent. Turnover was moderate at HK$883.22 million, brokers said.
"Wall Street's worries about interest rates again gives an excuse to take-profit," said one broker with a Singaporean house.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped a mere 0.37 of a point to 5,888.83, while U.S. investors digested hints from a senior U.S. Federal Reserve official that a hike in lending rates was likely.
Hong Kong brokers appear similarly unfazed, and positive on the outlook for the market, analysts said.
"I'm still bullish. I think the market will recover in late afternoon," said Ho.
Ho said he believed new foreign funds had entered the market recently.
All sectors suffered profit-taking, with finance and H shares the hardest hit.
HSBC, which has been leading the market for most of 1996, shed HK$1.00 to trade at $139.50, just above its minor support level at HK$139.00, analysts said.
"We are still expecting HSBC to rise to HK$150.00 by the end of the year," said the Singaporean broker.
Hang Seng Bank lost HK$0.50 to HK$81.00 and Bank of East Asia declined HK$0.25 to HK$28.35.
The share prices of property counters remained relatively resilient in the face of early selling pressure.
Properties remained relatively resilient in the face of early selling pressure.
Sun Hung Kai held steady at HK$79.00, while Henderson Land lost HK$0.25 to HK$65.00.
Conglomerate Swire Pacific, which gained HK$1.00 on Tuesday, eased HK$0.50 to HK$69.00.

China Light continued its strong performance, bucking the overall weak trend in the market. The share gained HK$0.40 to rise to HK$34.90. The company, whose year-end is September 30, is trading at a sizeable discount to the sector, analysts said.
